marks.gloss_en: R' Yehuda: only the animal's OWN mode acquires -- pulling for a camel, driving for a donkey
(entertained) if 'in this manner' excludes the reversed modes, the first tanna's position simply IS R' Yehuda's
Rav Ashi's text of the reins baraita: the rider-driver acquires the donkey and its halter; the reins-holder only what is in his hand; the rest neither
R' Abbahu: keep the baraita as taught -- the reins-holder acquires because he could yank them to himself
R' Eliezer: riding acquires in the field, leading in the city
Rav Kahana: riding fails in the city because people do not normally ride there
resolution: R' Eliezer's ruling concerns a sale, where the seller said 'acquire the way people acquire' (with carve-outs: public domain, an important person, a woman, a shameless one)
